summary: TRACK 14.0 PRODUCTION-TRUST-SUITE certification pass (iteration 512). Verified the four shipped fixes from iter511 (NewMeeting missingHint chip, HR Hub directory search, Safety Incidents CTA wiring, three router redirects) all hold. Exercised Phases 1, 2(c), 4 (signal-only), 5, 7, 9, 10, 11 (partial), 12 (iPad 1024x768), 14 (stress) end-to-end with cert.safety / cert.hr / cert.foreman fixtures. Pytest run: 6 passed, 3 failed (all 3 are 'wrong-endpoint-shape-in-test' or transient network — not product defects), 4 skipped. Trust verdict: Trusted ✓ (with caveats), Proven ✓ for the patched surfaces; surfaced ~10 substantive findings ranging from a P0 documented-credential mismatch to P3 visual-noise on coaching cards. No persistent TRUST-SUITE-CERT records were committed (meeting form Submit was deliberately not satisfied; no incident POSTed). Cap: 10 substantive findings (well under 25 ceiling).

critical.issue: Documented super-admin credential jaymn.judd@mascigc.com / Maddix123! returns 401 'Wrong password' on preview. Iter511 reported this worked via POST /sign-in (multi-login), but /api/sign-in itself returns 404. Either (a) Maddix123! was rotated on preview but /app/memory/test_credentials.md wasn't updated, or (b) the multi-login is wired through a different path (e.g. /api/login/master) that the credentials doc doesn't disclose. Trust-doctrine impact: a returning auditor following the credentials doc will hit 401 and assume the admin auth is broken.

minor.issue: Returns 405 Method Not Allowed (path with .csv suffix is being matched as POST-only or PUT-only route). The actual export lives at /api/admin/employees/export (no .csv suffix). If any frontend code path appends .csv to mirror the /api/incidents.csv convention, it will silently 405. Recommend either aliasing /api/admin/employees/export.csv to the GET handler OR documenting the canonical form.

/api/incidents accepts ONLY X-Safety-Token: <token> header for safety-portal tokens; it rejects 'Authorization: Bearer <safety_token>' with 401 'Safety, Admin, or PM login required'. The 401 message implies bearer should work. Inconsistent with /api/safety/login response (which returns just 'token', no header name guidance). Documentation/contract drift — not a runtime bug, but a trust-surface for any external integrator or new agent.

These intuitive aliases return 404 — the canonical route is /api/incidents only. No major harm but inconsistent with the directory/portal naming pattern used elsewhere (/api/hr/employees, /api/safety/trench-safety/*). Worth aliasing OR documenting the carve-out.

ui_bugs.issue: missingHint chip IS PRESENT and CORRECT (data-testid='meeting-submit-missing-hint' renders text 'MISSING: PROJECT NAME · LOCATION · CONDUCTED BY +4' on disabled-submit click). Iter511 fix CONFIRMED HOLDING at iPad 1024x768. NOTE: data-testid='submit-top-btn' .is_disabled() returned FALSE on page load even though Submit cannot succeed; the form gates submission post-click rather than via disabled-attribute. Acceptable UX, but flagged for awareness.

Bell badge shows '99+' for cert.hr@example.com — a freshly-minted cert fixture user. Either (a) 99+ is a legitimate cross-tenant notification fan-out that the cert user inherits (then the count is technically accurate but distrust-inducing), or (b) the count is stale/wrong. Phase 4 / Phase 5 require the count to match the bell-list contents — recommend a follow-up where main agent opens the bell list and asserts visible item count == 99 (or > 99 if paginated).

ui_bugs.component: Console error noise on /meetings/new and /hr (and likely other pages)
ui_bugs.issue: Every navigation to /meetings/new and /hr produces 6 console errors: '405 Method Not Allowed' x2 and '404 Not Found' x4 from background fetches (resource URLs not exposed in console but consistent across loads). Production-trust doctrine says 'no console-error storm'. Six errors per page-load on two of the most-visited surfaces is a measurable storm. Likely candidates: stale fetches to /api/admin/employees/export.csv, /api/hr/employees CSV/PDF endpoints, or notification-poller fetches.

ui_bugs.component: 5 COACHING TIPS card — repeated on multiple pages
ui_bugs.issue: Same visual block 'X COACHING TIPS AVAILABLE · TAP TO EXPAND' with the same 5 expandable rows appears on /meetings/new (Section 01) AND /hr/employees (top of main column). On the meeting form iter511 also flagged this duplicating within the same scroll. Not data-incorrect, but a visual-noise pattern that dilutes the trust hierarchy at iPad width where every vertical pixel matters.

ui_bugs.component: Toast 'Project Name is required' on disabled-submit click
ui_bugs.issue: Confirmed: clicking the disabled Submit on /meetings/new fires a toast 'Project Name is required' (visible in screenshot). GOOD — pairs cleanly with the missingHint chip in the header. PHASE 13 PASS: toast copy is specific, not generic 'Saved' / 'Done'.

integration_issues.issue: First-load navigation to /sign-in and /safety-sign-in timed out (10-12s) in 2 of 3 attempts (~40% flake). Subsequent reloads rendered the calm sign-in page in <2s. Possibly cold-start or edge cache miss on the preview deployment. Not blocking — but a 5:30 AM foreman who hits this will see a blank page for 10s and assume the platform is down.

design_issues.screen: Notification bell at iPad 1024x768 (HR portal header)
issues: Bell badge '99+' rendered in white-on-red — contrast OK, but at 1024px width the header crowds the bell + clock (6:55 PM) + EN/ES + HOME + SIGN OUT into the same row. Right-edge looks busy. No overflow bleed observed, but the visual hierarchy of the bell badge is low.

missingHint chip 'MISSING: PROJECT NAME · LOCATION · CONDUCTED BY +4' is RENDERED IN THE HEADER ROW next to SUBMIT — readable at iPad width ✓. Text truncates at '... +4' which is a clean affordance for the 4 hidden missing fields. Design holds at iPad.

Today the documented super-admin returns 401, which forces every downstream agent to discover the cert.* fixtures by trial and error.

P1: Investigate the 6 console errors per page-load on /meetings/new and /hr (2×405 + 4×404). Identify the failing fetches and either fix the URL or suppress the failure. Production-trust doctrine forbids a console-error storm.

P1: Verify the HR notification bell '99+' count matches the actual unread-notification list for cert.hr. If it doesn't match (e.g., bell list shows 3 items), this is a Phase 5 count-vs-list mismatch (CRITICAL trust defect).

P2: Alias /api/admin/employees/export.csv → /api/admin/employees/export (GET) so the .csv convention used elsewhere (e.g., /api/incidents.csv) is consistent — OR add a 410/200 sentinel so frontend probes don't get a confusing 405.

Today the 401 message 'Safety, Admin, or PM login required' is misleading when the request actually carries a valid safety token in the wrong header.
P3: De-dupe the COACHING TIPS card — it appears on /meetings/new AND /hr/employees AND (per iter511) twice within /meetings/new. Consolidate into a single dismissable surface per portal.

P3: Investigate intermittent 10-12s first-load timeouts on /sign-in and /safety-sign-in (~40% rate observed in this run). Could be cold-start; if so, add a server-side warmup or a client-side 'Loading sign-in...' affordance instead of blank screen.
critical_code_review_comments: NewMeeting.jsx: missingHint chip implementation is the right pattern. Suggest exposing the SAME hint as aria-describedby on the Submit button so screen readers narrate 'Submit — disabled — missing: PROJECT NAME, LOCATION, CONDUCTED BY (+4 more)'. Today only sighted users see the chip.

/app/frontend/src/lib/api.js (global error interceptor): the 405 + 404 console-error storm on /meetings/new and /hr suggests the interceptor is logging client-side fetches that fail. Consider classifying: 401 on /api/admin/* when no admin token is present should be SILENCED (it's expected), and 404 on probe endpoints likewise. Today every failed background probe pollutes console.

/app/backend/routes/safety.py: the 401 message 'Safety, Admin, or PM login required' on /api/incidents is correct when no token is present, but is MISLEADING when an Authorization: Bearer <safety_token> is sent. Consider extending the dependency to accept both X-Safety-Token AND Authorization: Bearer headers for the same token, OR change the 401 detail to 'Use X-Safety-Token header for safety-portal tokens'.

/app/memory/test_credentials.md: Stale. Iter506 already flagged the chriswright@/hrmanager@/testmech@/dispatch@ accounts as rotated. Now Maddix123! on jaymn.judd@ is also failing. Recommend a recurring (idempotent) test that asserts every documented credential still logs in successfully — drift this slow is undetectable until a future agent hits it.

rca of the issue: RCA — Documented super-admin credential failure: iter511 reported 'POST /sign-in worked first try' for jaymn.judd@mascigc.com / Maddix123! On iter512 the same payload to /api/sign-in returns 404 (route does not exist on backend; the auth endpoints are /api/admin/login, /api/safety/login, /api/hr/login, etc per backend/routes inventory). When the credential is POSTed to /api/admin/login directly, it returns 401 'Wrong password'. Two non-exclusive root causes: (1) The 'multi-login' wrapper iter511 used was a frontend-orchestrated POST that fan-out tried each portal endpoint sequentially, and admin happened to succeed back then; password has since been rotated. (2) The /sign-in frontend route hits an endpoint not present in backend/server.py search results — possibly an unmounted or feature-flagged route. Mitigation: main agent should (a) rotate Maddix123! back on preview using scripts/seed_admin.py, (b) confirm /sign-in frontend route is wired to a valid backend handler (or remove the route if dead), (c) add an idempotent CI check that POST /api/admin/login with documented credentials returns 200 — drift like this should fail loud, not silently force agents to fall back to cert.* fixtures.
